title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — if Adam sinned loco nostro, why not also punished loco with corruption at once?
pass_a_gloss: Placeus presses: if Adam sinned loco nostro and that act earned corruption as penalty, why wasn't he also hit with that penalty loco nostro? The instant he sinned he became corrupt, vicious, and unjust.
pass_b_english: Besides: if he sinned in our place, and that sin merited the penalty which is sin—namely corruption—tell me, I ask, why was he not also afflicted with that penalty in our place? For at the very moment he sinned, in the same he was made corrupt and vicious and unjust.
source_text: Praeterea si loco nostro peccavit & peccatum illud merebatur poenam quae est peccatum, videlicet corruptionem: dic mihi, quaeso, cur non sit etiam loco nostro illa affectus poena? nam quo temporis articulo peccavit, eodem corruptus & vitiosus & iniustus factus est.

choices.choice: Loco sin should bring loco corruption-penalty at once
